title: Inquest jury rules woman died of natural causes in Saskatchewan RCMP cell
article: A jury at a coroner's inquest has ruled that a woman died of natural causes two years ago in an RCMP cell in eastern Saskatchewan.
Deanna Whitecap was found unresponsive at the Indian Head detachment on Sept. 2, 2017, and was declared dead in hospital.
The cause of death was not identified.
Whitecap had been arrested and was being held on charges of driving while prohibited and suspected impairment.
The jury put forth eight recommendations for improving safety in similar situations.
The suggestions include increased monitoring of inmates and training to help guards determine when intoxicated inmates should be hospitalized rather than locked up.
The RCMP say they will be taking the recommendations into account and decide if they would be helpful moving forward.
Whitecap was in the custody of the File Hills First Nation Police Service that often shares RCMP facilities in Indian Head.
The inquest heard that emergency personnel who arrived about 2 1/2 minutes after a distress call found Whitecap unresponsive with no pulse or electrical activity.
The jury was shown a video of Whitecap giving a statement to police just hours before she died. She was to be released later in the day following her interview with police.
